scope: Proposition 7.1 (Subcubic realization) of the manuscript “Variable-dimension Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence on general and subcubic graphs” (preprints/Variable-dimension-Weisfeiler-Leman-equivalence-on-general-and-subcubic-graphs-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 133 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5b3048ce062b1b8e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: From the block data one can construct graphs X0, X1, with partitions V (Xε ) = ∐ B∈B V ε B (ε ∈ {0, 1}), having the following properties. 1. Both graphs are finite, simple, connected, uncolored, and of maximum degree at most three. They have the same positive order. Their orders are O(N4), and the construction is polynomial in the size of the explicitly listed block data. 2. For each z ∈ Zε B, the part V ε B contains a specified triangle Tε B(z). These triangles are pairwise disjoint. For every ξB ∈ Z1 B, there is a fixed bijection ΨB,ξB : V 0 B −→ V 1 B depending only on B, ξB, and the constructed graphs. It sends T0 B(z) onto T1 B(z + ξB). If U ⊆ B and the offsets (ξB)B∈U agree on all names shared by blocks in U, then the following map is an isomorphism of induced subgraphs: ∐ B∈U ΨB,ξB : X0 [ ⋃ B∈U V 0 B ] −→ X1 [ ⋃ B∈U V 1 B ] . 3. Fix a winning Duplicator strategy in the K-slot bijection game, where K = r + 1 ≥ 9. At every reached history, a marked vertex in T0 B(z) is paired with a vertex in T1 B(z′) for a unique z′ ∈ Z1 B. If simultaneous marked vertices lie in T0 B(z) and T0 C(w), where B ̸= C, then, for each ρ ∈ R(B) ∩ R(C), z|ρ = w|ρ =⇒ z′ |ρ = w′ |ρ. These conclusions hold even when all K slots are occupied.
